source.author: stat
source.text: iam semina pugnae ipse dedi: remeat portans immania Tydeus ausa, ducis scelus et, turpis primordia belli, insidias fraudesque, suis quas ultus in armis, adde fidem, vos o superi, meus ordine sanguis, ne pugnare odiis, neu me temptare precando certetis; sic Fata mihi nigraeque Sororum iuravere colus: manet haec ab origine mundi fixa dies bello, populique in proelia nati.
source.text_original: iam semina pugnae / ipse dedi: remeat portans immania Tydeus / ausa, ducis scelus et, turpis primordia belli, / insidias fraudesque, suis quas ultus in armis, / adde fidem, vos o superi, meus ordine sanguis, / ne pugnare odiis, neu me temptare precando / certetis; sic Fata mihi nigraeque Sororum / iuravere colus: manet haec ab origine mundi / fixa dies bello, populique in proelia nati.
source.text_english: Already I myself have given the seeds of battle: Tydeus returns bearing monstrous deeds, the crime of the leader and, shameful beginnings of war, the ambushes and treacheries, which he has avenged in his own armor. Add faith, O gods above, you my blood in due order: do not strive to fight with hatred, nor to assail me with prayers; so the Fates and the dark distaffs of the Sisters have sworn to me. This day, fixed for war from the world’s beginning, remains for the people born to battle.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Tum genitor vetera haec nobis et condita pergunt ordine cuncta suo rerumque a principe cursu fixa manent; neque enim terris tum sanguis in ullis noster erat, cum fata darem, iustique facultas hinc mihi, cum varios struerem per saecula reges.
reuse.text_original: Tum genitor 'vetera haec nobis et condita pergunt / ordine cuncta suo rerumque a principe cursu / fixa manent; neque enim terris tum sanguis in ullis / noster erat, cum fata darem, iustique facultas / hinc mihi, cum varios struerem per saecula reges.
reuse.text_english: Then our father tells us these ancient things and all things, once established, continue in their own order and remain fixed in the course of events from the beginning of the world; for there was not yet any blood of ours on any lands when I was granting destinies, and from this came my power to rule justly, when I was setting up different kings through the ages.
